The FHN structure consists of three layers: flexible aluminum foil (0.150 mm), polyimide film with FSS pattern (135 μm), and nanocomposite absorber sheet.
The nanocomposite sheet uses graphite nanopowder (400 nm) and zinc oxide powder (600 nm) fillers in a polyurethane matrix.
The fabricated nanocomposite sheet shows dielectric loss tangents between 0.25 and 0.45 in the X-band frequency range.
The FSS pattern is printed on a flexible polyimide substrate with dielectric constant 3.5 and loss tangent 0.002.
Simulated reflection coefficient of the FSS alone shows a minimum of 0.08 magnitude at 11.20 GHz, corresponding to 98.74% absorption.
The overall thickness of the FHN absorber is 1.335 mm.
The FHN structure achieves a minimum reflection coefficient of −28 dB at 10.2 GHz.
The −10 dB reflection coefficient bandwidth covers the entire X-band (8–12 GHz).
Increasing the nanocomposite thickness from 1.0 to 1.4 mm shifts the reflection minima to lower frequencies.
The fabricated FHN structure provides at least 10 dB RCS reduction on cylindrical targets under various polarizations.
The reflection coefficient threshold of −10 dB corresponds to 90% absorption and 56% RCS reduction.
The nanocomposite fabrication involved sonification, curing at 70 °C for 2 hours, and 24-hour postcuring at room temperature.
The free-space measurement technique with focused horn lens antennas was used to characterize complex permittivity.
The FSS unit cell geometry and interelement spacing critically affect bandwidth, polarization, and incidence angle performance.
The combination of graphite and zinc oxide fillers provides high dielectric constant and loss tangent, enhancing microwave absorption.
The FHN design leverages impedance matching from FSS and dielectric losses from nanocomposite for wideband stealth applications.
The study includes detailed electromagnetic analysis and material morphology characterization to understand absorption mechanisms.
Previous absorbers like Salisbury screen and Jaumann layers have limitations in thickness and bandwidth addressed by this FHN approach.
The FHN structure is flexible and lightweight, suitable for strategic outdoor stealth applications requiring conformal coverage.
The research uses CST Microwave Studio for 3-D electromagnetic simulation under periodic boundary conditions.
